title: Per-path telemetry and cost allocation for vector search + rerank
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Provide per-path (per-route / per-endpoint) telemetry and dollar/token cost attribution for embedding and reranking flows so teams can diagnose quality regressions, latency hotspots, and the unit economics of vector search + rerank.

Scope:
- Instrument embedding + rerank pipeline so a single request flow emits a correlated trace containing: HTTP parent span, embedding model spans (with model name, token count, vector dim), vector index lookup spans (shard id, hit counts), rerank model spans (candidate count, prompt size), and scoring spans.
- Expose per-route Grafana dashboards with: p50/p95 latency breakdown by span, per-request token and vector cost estimates, QPS and concurrency, recall/quality signals (sampled embeddings similarity, rerank NDCG on eval set), and cost per 1k requests.
- Add alerting rules for anomalies: sustained p95 increase in embed or rerank spans, cost-per-request spike >20% vs baseline, and fall in sampled rerank quality metrics.
- Provide lightweight sampling + async ingest to avoid adding tail latency.

Non-goals: End-to-end retraining or auto-tuning of models based on these signals (follow-up work). Full per-customer billing integration is out of scope; we provide per-route cost estimates only.

Implementation approach:
1) Tracing: extend runtime request context to add explicit span names and attributes for embedding and rerank operations. Use existing OpenTelemetry pipeline; add attribute conventions ("ri.model.name", "ri.embed.dim", "ri.rerank.candidates").
2) Cost model: implement a deterministic estimator that maps model name + token counts + embedding dims to a cost-per-call string metric. Costs will be based on current pricing table (console-2026.03 rates) and emitted as metrics (gauge) per request and as delta counters aggregated in dashboards.
3) Dashboards: new Grafana folder "Embeddings / Rerank - Per Path" with templated panels for any route. Default panels: Span waterfall, Token/cost histogram, Quality sampling chart, Top slow routes, Top expensive routes.
4) Alerting: add Prometheus rules in the same alerting group as runtime SLOs. Alerts will include runbook links and suggested mitigation (switch to cheaper model, reduce candidate set, enable KV cache for recent queries).
5) Rollout: beta on a small subset of internal routes (internal-search, docs-query), canary to 5% customer traffic, then wide rollout. Provide SDK flag to opt-out of sampling for privacy-sensitive customers.

Trade-offs / decisions:
- Sampling: to avoid cost and latency overhead we sample full embedding vectors for quality signals at 1% by default. This trades statistical confidence for runtime cost.
- Cardinality: adding model name and route labels increases metrics cardinality. We'll limit label combinations and use hashed route IDs in high-cardinality contexts.
- Cost accuracy vs simplicity: estimator will be an approximation (rounded per 100 tokens) to keep metric ingestion cheap.

Deliverables:
- PR implementing span attributes and cost estimator in runtime (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime PR#1314)
- Grafana dashboard templates and provisioning JSON
- Prometheus alerting rules and runbooks
- Confluence playbook describing interpretation and runbooks
- Post-rollout retrospective and cost/latency regression dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Traces show separate spans for embedding and rerank ops with agreed attribute schema
Per-route Grafana dashboard can be instantiated for any route and shows latency and cost breakdown
Prometheus alerts fire on synthetic regressions in test environment and have functioning runbooks
Cost-per-request estimator matches manual calculations within 10% for our benchmark routes
Sampling and tracing changes add <1% tail latency on 99th percentile in canary
risks: Metric cardinality growth leading to Prometheus pressure if route/model label combinations are not controlled
Sampling may miss rare quality regressions — need to surface and tune sampling configs
Privacy concerns if sampled vectors are stored for quality checks — ensure masking/encryption and retention limits
Estimator drift as pricing changes, requires a process to update and version the pricing table
